newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil eases on futures and ample supply.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil eases on futures and ample supply.

text.p: NWE gas oil eased on Wednesday in line with sinking benchmark IPE futures, although traders said the price dip had encouraged some German shortcovering.
June IPE gas oil settled $1.25 lower at $168.75 a tonne.
Heating oil barges traded at June IPE +$1.0 fob ARA and June IPE +$1.25 fob Rotterdam for first half June delivery. Traders assessed premiums at June IPE +$1.0/++$1.75 fob ARA.

Low sulphur was under pressure as Mediterranean cargoes hit the north. Barge premiums were quoted at June IPE +$7.0/+$9.0 fob ARA for first half June delivery -- the highest heard done was at June IPE +$8.50 fob ARA.
Traders had mixed feelings about the apparent low sulphur glut. "Everywhere you turn there's material on offer," said one trader. Others noted that it would not take much to change the situation.
"The Far East arb appears to be open, there's not much Med material left to commit to the north so it's not as if we're going to see a never-ending stream of material," said another.

The U.S. trader who bought three low sulphur cargoes on Tuesday at June IPE +$6.0, +$6.50 and +$5.25 fob cif was reported to have sold fourth quarter swaps at $10.50 over contemporaneous 0.2 percent swap prices.
